title: Var, Let, Const & Hoisting: No Surprises

scenes.line1: Why do some variables throw errors
scenes.say: Ever wonder why some variables throw errors before they're declared, but others just show up as undefined?
Here's the deal: var is function-scoped and gets hoisted and initialized. Let and const are block-scoped, also hoisted, but not initialized right away.
Between entering a block and actually declaring let or const, you hit the temporal dead zone. Try to use them early, and you'll get a Reference Error.
Check this out. Logging a before it's declared gives you undefined, but logging b throws a Reference Error. That's hoisting and the temporal dead zone in action.

scenes.question: Which is safer for new code?
scenes.right: Stick to let and const to avoid bugs from hoisting and scope confusion.
scenes.say: In interviews, don't fall for the trap—using let and const helps you avoid subtle bugs from hoisting and scoping issues.
